📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase.
  • The update, of course, also adds new content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.
  • We’ve known about the latest content side of today’s patch for quite some time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major enhancement earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The update, of course, also adds new content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

We’ve known about the latest content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The enhancement kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a newly introduced limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other big new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

These are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

Redsec players have a new Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

According to recent reports, the fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a massive overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

Industry observers note that controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this update, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several problems that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

In a recent development, certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

#224537. Why Cancer Biomarker Testing Is Personal for Mark-Paul Gosselaar

Why Cancer Biomarker Testing Is Personal for Mark-Paul Gosselaar

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1096 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Known for his iconic roles on “Saved by the Bell,” “NYPD Blue,” “Franklin & Bash,” and “Found,” Mark-Paul Gosselaar knows how to grab an audience.
  • Now, he’s using that star power to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing while sharing how he prioritizes his own health and well-being.
  • “Health is a huge thing for my wife and I, and our family,” Gosselaar told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Known for his iconic roles on “Saved by the Bell,” “NYPD Blue,” “Franklin & Bash,” and “Found,” Mark-Paul Gosselaar knows how to grab an audience.

Now, he’s using that star power to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing while sharing how he prioritizes his own health and well-being.

“Health is a huge thing for my wife and I, and our family,” Gosselaar told Healthline. “We are constantly aware of latest technologies.”.

Having seen people in his life navigate cancer diagnoses, Gosselaar is now raising awareness about the role of biomarker testing in cancer treatment through his partnership with AstraZeneca and its Meet Your Mark campaign.

It has been revealed that the campaign aims to educate people facing cancer diagnoses and their loved ones about how biomarker testing may help doctors make more informed, personalized treatment decisions. It also encourages patients to discuss testing with their healthcare teams.

“Biomarkers may tell doctors the specific type of cancer present and if targeted therapies or immunotherapy might help,” Mark Socinski, MD, oncologist and Executive Medical Director of the AdventHealth Cancer Institute, told Healthline.

Recent findings suggest that he explained that biomarkers are typically genes or proteins that doctors measure through blood or tissue tests. They are used to help guide treatment in numerous diseases but are especially powerful tools in many types of cancer.

“They help decode why cancers behave differently, even when two people have the same cancer type,” said Socinski. “However, while biomarker testing provides useful information, it does not guarantee a specific outcome.”.

Despite those limitations, Socinski sees promise in the shift from one-size-fits-all cancer treatment to care tailored to each patient’s specific cancer characteristics.

In a recent development, “Biomarker testing does play a critical role here, and it is notable for people to be aware of the potential benefits,” Socinski said. “It may help change the course of a person’s treatment journey.”.

Gosselaar hopes that greater awareness of biomarker testing can help people facing a cancer diagnosis feel more informed about their treatment options.

“A lot of the time, when a loved one or someone who has been diagnosed with cancer [it can] feel like your world is in a tailspin,” he stated. “I wanted to get the word out for anyone who’s going through a cancer diagnosis, or a caretaker, to know that biomarker testing is an option, because even though two cancers are similar, their tumors can act very differently and biomarker testing may help the medical expert with more personalized treatment.”.

As part of the campaign, Gosselaar took part in a commercial, something he hadn’t done since before his days on “Saved by the Bell.”.

“This was the first time that I actually had to be on set and not be a character; I had to be me talking about this very serious matter,” he mentioned.

While it was a challenging experience, he remarked it was also fulfilling.

According to recent reports, “I enjoyed the process, and to be able to use my platform to be able to spread the word; it means a lot to me,” he mentioned. “I’m very selective of the things that I want to attach myself to, and this seemed like the right fit.”.

He particularly enjoyed recreating Zack Morris’s signature “timeout” gesture from “Saved by the Bell,” which allowed his character to freeze time and speak directly to the camera.

“Using something from the past that was such a symbolic gesture to so many people of my generation that are now my age and possibly going through [cancer] or knowing someone who’s going through [cancer to] direct them to [this campaign], means a lot,” he said.

Beyond his efforts to raise awareness about cancer biomarker testing, Gosselaar is equally focused on taking care of his own health.

Industry observers note that getting quality sleep is one of his top priorities. He sleeps on a high-tech mattress that monitors sleep stages, heart rate, heart rate variability, and respiratory rate. He also uses a biometric health and fitness tracker, prioritizes healthy eating, and uses saunas and red light therapy.

“We do everything that we possibly can, but I’m less about longevity and more about just living a healthy lifestyle,” Gosselaar remarked. “I want to continue doing the things that I’ve done since I was a child…without feeling held back by my health.”.

According to recent reports, as he embraces his 50s, he mentioned he’d like to live a long life for his children and future grandchildren. He started taking his health seriously in his 40s after undergoing shoulder surgery.

“[It] really made me realize [that] all the damage I had done in my 20s and 30s sort of adds up later in life, and that’s probably something that I would tell the younger me… to preserve a little bit more and take [an] approach that recovery is just as vital as the workout because I did not use my recovery very well; it was not a priority for me,” said Gosselaar.

Recent findings suggest that he also makes time for himself every day. He remarked doing so makes him a better person and more able to care for his wife and four children.

Sources indicate that “[It’s] something that I believe in; that I need to do something for myself before I can do something for someone else. Or if I do something for someone else, then I have to equalize that by doing something for me,” he said.

Daily physical activity also helps support his mental well-being.

“I need to do something where I challenge myself, and it could be as simple as a walk. It could be as simple as just getting outside and lifting something heavy [or] taking bags of groceries and taking the long way into your house,” Gosselaar remarked.

“Like challenging yourself with picking up things, you know, taking backpacks from the car from your kids and seeing if you can carry three in one hand…or going into the gym and spending an hour in the gym, or 30 minutes, or just moving.”.

When he’s in the sauna, he works on breathing and clearing his thoughts.

According to recent reports, “Some people need to meditate, some people need to talk to somebody. I encourage all of that because I think all of that helps,” he remarked.

“I’ve done them all. I’ve done the cold plunging, I’ve done all that stuff…some of it works, and some of it doesn’t; it’s whatever you believe in. So I just encourage people to stay healthy and move, get outside, and help other people.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that are you a port or rail terminal operator looking for a new electric material handler that can move serious cargo without sacrificing maneuverability? Do you wish it had tank treads? If that’s you, the Mantsinen 200 might be just the thing.

Designed to handle demanding port and rail terminal operations, the Finnish-built Matsinen 200 material handler combines impressive reach and lifting capacity with the ability to move around a worksite on its own tracks. And, yes: I said tracks.

It has been revealed that by far the most fun feature of the Mantsinen 200 is the fact that it looks like a rejected concept for a ROBOTIX dinosaur set and/or something He-Man would use to run over Trap Jaw. And while, yes – most big material handlers have similar form factors, there’s something about the 200 that really sells the whole Dragon Walker vibe.

Industry observers note that the Mantsinen 200 is powered by a 380 kW (~510 hp) grid-connected electric motor running at 1,800 rpm. Power comes from a 460V electrical connection as standard, with other voltage options available to suit local site requirements.

According to recent reports, mantsinen says its electrically powered machines deliver the same performance as their diesel counterparts, while eliminating exhaust emissions at the machine and reducing operating noise, energy consumption and maintenance costs. Power is delivered through a load-sensing hydraulic system featuring four variable-displacement piston pumps and a separate closed-loop swing circuit.

It has been revealed that mantsinen also fits the 200 with its proprietary HybriLift energy-recovery system. HybriLift works a lot like regenerative braking by capturing potential energy as the main boom is lowered, but instead of storing that energy as electricity in a battery, the material handler stores it in hydraulic accumulators for reuse during the next lift. The company claims HybriLift improves the big machine’s energy efficiency by up to 50%, effectively giving the machine an additional 300 (ish) hp of lifting assistance at average lifting speed.

In a recent development, and, while the machine normally draws power from the grid, operators aren’t necessarily tethered to an outlet. Mantsinen offers an optional PowerPack that allows the machine to disconnect from its main power supply and still travel around the worksite, with some basic hydraulic systems still functional. The PowerPack is right now diesel-powered, but a battery-backed version isn’t out of the question. It’s a useful bit of flexibility for terminal operators who want the benefits of electric material handling without giving up the ability to reposition the machine when a fixed electrical connection isn’t available.

According to recent reports, what do you guys think – is this major material handler the thing you need for your logging or scrapyard, or are you holding out for something even bigger? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “We don’t know how the injury happened, but we’re impressed by the bear’s resilience,” the rangers write.
  • Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the annual Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Resilience and perseverance was on full display in Alaska this summer. The park rangers at Tongass National Forest in the southeastern corner of the state spotted an unnamed black bear (Ursus americanus) with a broken arm. Even with this injury, the tough bear still managed to catch the fish running through Anan Creek. For this grit, the rangers awarded the bear with the 2026 Grin & Bear It Award.

“We don’t know how the injury happened, but we’re impressed by the bear’s resilience,” the rangers write. “In other wild places the injury may have been a death sentence, but the abundance of Anan gives this bear a chance.”.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the annual Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

The largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area also includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears like the one with the broken arm and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their portly counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own behaviors and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

This is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

It has been revealed that the Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

Instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two fresh maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

As for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

It has been revealed that beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two upcoming maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

It has been revealed that the miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for fresh players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

Tech Report: Psychedelic therapies may improve decision making

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health challenges like anxiety and depression.
  • According to recent reports, the team’s experiment was straightforward.
  • According to recent reports, while the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health challenges like anxiety and depression. Although they’re commonly associated with mind-altering trips and sometimes confounding experiences, recent research indicates small doses may provide an opposite outcome. In a study published today in the journal Science Advances, researchers show that psychedelics may actually improve decision making in certain situations.

According to recent reports, the team’s experiment was straightforward. After supplying lab mice with small amounts of ketamine or psilocybin, neuroscientists exposed them to a simple, sensory-based training exercise. Each mouse was tasked with identifying which of two sites contained a reward based on light pulses emitted from either location. Researchers then compared their decisions with a control group of mice who didn’t receive either psychedelic.

According to recent reports, while the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue. However, the mice treated with ketamine or psilocybin appeared to rely less on repetition and more on sensory observations. As a result, they had fewer errors and found the location more effectively.

“These findings reveal how psychedelics reduce the reliance on habits and repetitive choices, which may explain part of their therapeutic effect,” Benjamin Scott, a Boston University psychologist and study co-author, stated in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) have remained the most commonly prescribed anxiety and depression medications for decades, but they often come with caveats. Patients usually take SSRIs for weeks before experiencing any relief, and they must take them consistently for indefinite periods of time. Meanwhile, about 30 percent of people with depression are resistant to SSRIs, which makes treatment much more difficult. Another benefit is that the effects of ketamine and psilocybin are much easier to map in the brain compared to SSRIs, even after a half century of research.

“We know a great deal about how psychedelics affect the nervous system,” stated Scott.

Recent findings suggest that on a molecular level, psychedelics bind to receptors on neurons, protective neural cells called glia, and likely other cells. Once attached, the effects compound throughout the brain by altering cellular activity, circuits, and neuroactivity. Psilocybin works with serotonin receptors to influence how information is processed. In contrast, ketamine is a dissociative psychedelic that functions as an antagonist to specific receptors.

Recent findings suggest that “The discovery we report in this paper is that these two drugs have similar pro-cognitive effects, at least in mice performing a simple task,” Scott explained. “Both drugs strengthen the influence of sensory evidence on choices and reduce the effect of bias.”.

According to recent reports, the study’s authors do note some potentially negative effects, as well. Although a mouse’s accuracy improved, the correct decisions sometimes came more slowly than before they took the psychedelics. Scott said this may logically translate to impacts on human reaction times, which could be a problem during activities like driving a car or playing sports. Despite this, the team is still confident in what psychedelics have already accomplished for patients, as well as what that could mean in the future. Scott cited existing evidence of patients reporting noticeable, long-lasting improvements after a single dose of psilocybin.

“This is dramatically different than today’s first-line drugs for depression,” he added.

#224530. 5 Things We’re Saying No to This Holiday Season

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (958 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

5 Things We’re Saying No to This Holiday Season

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (958 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to.
  • Recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to. Consider the feelings that come up for you when you think about it. Is it excitement about seeing the people you love? Is it dread at the anticipation of planning, conflict, or grief? For some, it’s all of the above.

Recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S. adults report holiday stressors (APA, 2023). Tensions arise due to finances, family conflict, grief, and other factors. Stress takes away from the pleasurable aspects of the season, which should include reconnection and rest.

According to recent reports, sometimes that is easier said than done. Here are 5 things we're saying no to this holiday season and strategies to achieve the happy holidays we deserve.

In a recent development, sometimes that family holiday announcement sounds like a demand rather than an invitation. “Dinner is at 4 pm sharp. See you there!” Everyone assumes you’ll be there, and no one asks questions. They don’t ask if you can take time off work, afford the trip, or have other aims. You feel obligated to attend despite any barriers you are facing.

Sources indicate that almost no one will tell you that you are allowed to consider your own needs before you RSVP yes. Ask yourself whether you have the time, energy, and money to participate this year. If the answer is no, it’s alright. Your family may be disappointed, and you may feel a little guilty, but it’s worth asking which will weigh on you more: the guilt of saying no or the cost of saying yes.

Industry observers note that in toxic families, it’s the once-over as soon as you enter the room. Before you’ve even had a chance to sit down, someone has made a joke about your weight or graying hair, offered a backhanded compliment about the dish you contributed, or slipped in a dig about your personal life.

You may feel hurt, sad, or even angry, and you don’t have to ignore those feelings to preserve the holiday spirit. You can be silent and stone-faced to let the “joke” fall flat. You might excuse yourself and regroup in another room. If you want to address it directly and call out the hidden meaning, you can say, “That felt like a dig,” or ask, “What do you mean by that?” What you don’t have to do is tolerate disrespect.

When you want everyone to feel loved, it’s easy to slip into spending more than you intended. If you’ve ever hosted a large family gathering, you know how swiftly the groceries and gifts add up. And if you’re the one who hosts every year, it can feel like the work and the bill are yours by default.

Before you do anything, set a budget. Then share the work in ways that play into everyone’s strengths. Maybe enlist the nephew who can roast meat or the cousin who loves to bake, and assign cleanup to the one you prefer to stay out of the kitchen. Suggest rotating hosting duties. Do a gift exchange rather than buying individual gifts for everyone. You can show your love to your family with limits.

According to recent reports, in some families, playing the dutiful daughter (or son) means everyone assumes you’ll make the holidays happen. Often it’s the family matriarch or the eldest daughter who initiates the first call about the holiday looks and is the one still in the kitchen long after everyone else has gone home. She is the family “glue” who keeps track of the invites, remembers who can’t eat what, and figures out where to seat the relatives who aren’t speaking. By the time the holiday arrives, she’s too tired to enjoy the fruits of her labor.

If that sounds like you, name it. People who have never hosted may not realize all of the hidden effort that goes into an event. Bring it to their attention. Set limits on what you will do and ask for help, but don’t micromanage. If the person assigned to bring the rolls forgets, skip the rolls this year. If no one steps up, step back anyway. Initiative a smaller, more intimate gathering that won’t leave you frazzled at the end of it.

Sources indicate that the holidays aren’t the same after you’ve lost a loved one, and the first holiday season after a loss can be especially difficult. Family traditions may be upended. The person who always hosted and made everyone’s favorite dish is gone. Tensions that surface after the loss may still be hanging in the air.

In a recent development, take a moment to evaluate your feelings. Ask yourself what you feel up to this year. Maybe it’s not the year to take on hosting duties, or perhaps you stop by for dessert rather than staying the entire day. You can choose to honor your loved one by retaining old traditions or step into the next chapter with new traditions in their memory. You can miss someone deeply and still make room for moments of joy this holiday season.

According to recent reports, it might seem strange that saying no could be the start of a happy holiday. The beauty is that you get to decide what a happy holiday looks like for you, and that it can change from year to year. Ask yourself what would make the holidays feel good to you this year and do it.

American Psychological Association. (2023). Even a joyous holiday season can cause stress for most Americans. https://www.apa.org/news/press/releases/2023/11/holiday-season-stress.

The FIA began the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend by announcing that all manufacturers have agreed to the framework to bring turbocharged V8 engines back to F1 and move away from the current V6 turbo.

This move has long been expected, with hopes that it will make engine building easier and cheaper while bringing back the sound that motorsport fans deeply miss.

The sound of the V8 engines was a rally cry for fans and has been sorely missed by audiences worldwide.

The F1 engine manufacturers agreed to a rough-out overarching proposal to move to a 2.1-liter turbocharged V8 from 2030 onwards, with a lower charge of electrical power reducing the hybrid output from 350kW to 200kW, a decrease of nearly 56 percent.

The FIA announced that ‘The blueprint is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing.”.

With everyone in agreement, PU manufacturers will start to jockey between improving the new car entering a sophomore season of new regulations and game planning for the major change coming just three seasons down the line.

It’s been 13 years since manufacturers last built a V8 engine for F1.

Sources indicate that “This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1,” FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said. “From the outset, I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability.

“The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this Championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide. Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition.”.

According to recent reports, victoria Beaver is a nomadic sports writer who spends her time hopping between race tracks and hippie farms. She’s covered every corner of motorsports that will let her in from 410 Sprints to NASCAR to Supercross. Her daily driver is a 2010 Subaru that she refused to do the smallest amount of preventative maintenance on. Instead, she spends her free time and money building a 42-foot Skoolie to one day travel the country full time.

GLP-1s May Help Lower Diabetes, Heart Risks Better Than Standard Prevention

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 drugs are more effective in helping prevent type 2 diabetes than the commonly prescribed medication metformin, according to a new study.
  • Researchers stated GLP-1s such as Ozempic and Mounjaro were more likely to reduce blood sugar to healthy levels in people with prediabetes and obesity.
  • They added that people prescribed GLP-1 medications had a lower risk of progressing from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 drugs are more effective in helping prevent type 2 diabetes than the commonly prescribed medication metformin, according to a new study.

Researchers stated GLP-1s such as Ozempic and Mounjaro were more likely to reduce blood sugar to healthy levels in people with prediabetes and obesity.

They added that people prescribed GLP-1 medications had a lower risk of progressing from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.

The researchers noted that GLP-1 customers also had a lower risk of death from any cause as well as fewer heart attacks, strokes, and heart failure events compared with metformin users.

“The great news with prediabetes is that it’s still possible to reverse the progression of the disease,” mentioned Vinicius de Sousa Barzon Serra, MD, a study author and research fellow in cardiovascular medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale, Arizona, in a press release. “This research may add to the case for considering GLP-1 medications earlier for certain patients, rather than waiting until they develop type 2 diabetes.”.

Serra noted that metformin still remains an effective treatment for people with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes.

“This is less about replacing one medication with another and more about discussing additional options with specific patients,” he said.

It has been revealed that the researchers presented their findings at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2026 in Chicago. The research has not been published yet in a peer-reviewed journal.

David Cutler, MD, a family medicine physician at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, wasn’t involved in the study, but mentioned the findings were “quite impressive.”.

“It elevates the comfort of prescribing GLP-1 drugs as a front-line treatment,” he told Healthline.

Robert Eckel, MD, a former president of the American Heart Association who was likewise not involved in the study, agrees the research provides more options for patients and prescribers.

“GLP-1s provide another option for prevention, perhaps as an add-on therapy. However, costs and access to these medications are notable factors,” said Eckel, an endocrinologist at the University of Colorado School of Medicine, in the press release.

For their study, the researchers analyzed the medical records of 256,000 adults in the United States with prediabetes and obesity. About 76% of the subjects were women, and the average age of the participants was 52.

About half of those studied were taking GLP-1 drugs with the active ingredient semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, or dulaglutide.

The other half had been prescribed metformin, a medication used to help manage blood sugar levels in adults and some children with type 2 diabetes by decreasing glucose production in the liver, reducing glucose absorption from food, and improving the body’s insulin sensitivity.

The researchers reported that the people in the study who were taking GLP-1 drugs had a 1.5 times higher chance of reversing high blood sugar to healthy levels compared to people who were using metformin.

The researchers also noted that GLP-1 medication consumers had a 31% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes and a 41% lower risk of death from any cause.

They added that GLP-1 medications were associated with 15% fewer heart attacks, 20% fewer strokes, 25% fewer cases of heart failure, and 8% fewer cases of atrial fibrillation (AFib), a common type of irregular heartbeat.

It has been revealed that the researchers cautioned that their study is observational and, therefore, cannot prove a cause-and-effect relationship. They also noted they relied on prescription records, so the frequency and dosage at which patients took their medication was not reflected.

In addition, the GLP-1 drugs were grouped together, so individual differences between medications were not considered.

Eckel mentioned in the news release that the benefits for people taking GLP-1 drugs were probably mainly due to weight loss. Eckel noted that the research results open up a wide range of possibilities.

“This is an key finding because the GLP-1 receptor agonists are commonly used today and this is a population that in the transition from prediabetes to diabetes are at increasing risk for cardiovascular disease,” Eckel said in a taped interview alongside the study findings.

In a recent development, cutler pointed out that several GLP-1 drugs also target blood sugar levels and insulin production. They could be effective in people with prediabetes who don’t have weight management issues.

Cutler noted that these people, however, might be reluctant to take GLP-1 drugs because they may not be experiencing symptoms of their prediabetes but could develop side effects with the medications.

According to recent reports, “They would not be getting any immediate benefits,” Cutler noted. He added that metformin, which was first used clinically in 1958, remains an effective alternative. “It’s been proven safe, effective, and it’s very cheap,” Cutler said.

It’s estimated that 40 million people in the United States have diabetes, with more than 90% of those cases being type 2 diabetes, a chronic condition characterized by high blood glucose levels that results from the body’s ineffective response to insulin or insufficient insulin production.

It’s also estimated that 115 million adults in the United States have prediabetes, a condition in which a person has higher-than-normal blood sugar levels but not high enough to be diagnosed as type 2 diabetes.

It has been revealed that around 5–10% of people with prediabetes develop diabetes every year. More broadly, up to 70% of people with prediabetes eventually develop diabetes.

Medication is sometimes prescribed for people with type 2 diabetes and prediabetes. Lifestyle changes can help reverse type 2 diabetes and prediabetes, as well as prevent the progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.

Among those lifestyle modifications are:.

Cutler said the lifestyle changes needed to prevent type 2 diabetes are pretty clear.

“The most notable thing for people with prediabetes to know is they should lose weight, reduce their carbs, exercise daily and, if that doesn’t work, then consider medication,” he said.

  • Recent findings suggest that additionally, one otter can travel five to 10 miles a day along rivers and streams, making them difficult to track.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that el Capitan. Glowing waterfalls. Half dome. River otters. Yosemite National Park is home to all of these natural wonders and more. The plucky and playful mammals have officially been spotted in the population park in Northern California—and park rangers want the public’s help to monitor them.

Recent findings suggest that even for experienced rangers and biologists, North American river otters (Lontra canadensis) are difficult to monitor. They have a very high metabolism, and can eat about 15 to 20 percent of their body weight in a single day. They spend a lot of their time looking for prey, including fish, crayfish, crabs, frogs, birds’ eggs, and even some reptiles like turtles.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, one otter can travel five to 10 miles a day along rivers and streams, making them difficult to track. According to the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, river otters’ range stretches all of Northern California’s five coastal counties from Oregon down to San Francisco Bay, the Sierra Nevada Mountains from Mariposa County north, and large parts of the inland northern valley. Yosemite National Park itself has over 1,700 miles of streams, so that’s a lot of wet ground to cover when looking for otters.

Park rangers are asking the public to note the location, date, and time of any river otter sightings in Yosemite. Written sightings can be reported in the comments section of this Facebook post or the park’s contact us form. Any videos or photos can be shared through a direct message on Instagram.

“Your observations can help us better understand how otters roam and use Yosemite’s waterways,” the rangers write.

River otters are not endangered, but they have had a rocky history. During the 19th and 20th centuries, they were extensively hunted and trapped for their fur and many were removed from their natural range. Decades of conservation and reintroduction efforts are currently helping populations to recover. California’s population is considered fairly stable, but they are still at risk from further habitat destruction and water pollution.

#224526. A rare triple-star system near Earth ‘should not exist’

A rare triple-star system near Earth ‘should not exist’

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (500 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronomers searching for new exoplanets recently found something much stranger—a rarely seen triple-star system located only 28 light-years away from Earth.
  • “The system should not exist,” Patrick Dufour, a University of Montreal astrophysicist and study co-author, noted in a statement.
  • Dufour’s team first noticed the perplexing triple-star system while scanning for exoplanets using highly sensitive equipment mounted on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope near the dormant volcano of Mauna Kea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronomers searching for new exoplanets recently found something much stranger—a rarely seen triple-star system located only 28 light-years away from Earth. If that weren’t odd enough, two of its three stellar components are dense, depleted white dwarfs. A study recently published in the Astronomy & Astrophysics Journal details an oddball trio that is so perplexing that researchers still aren’t quite sure how it formed in the first place.

“The system should not exist,” Patrick Dufour, a University of Montreal astrophysicist and study co-author, noted in a statement. “We have no clean explanation for how it got here.”.

Dufour’s team first noticed the perplexing triple-star system while scanning for exoplanets using highly sensitive equipment mounted on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope near the dormant volcano of Mauna Kea. Astronomers were specifically looking for subtle discrepancies in the movements of distant stars, which often indicates that there are orbiting planets nearby.

But when it came to one particular red dwarf, the data simply didn’t make sense. Rather than delicate shifts in motion, researchers recorded velocity swings at speeds nearing 10 miles per second. This effect was too much for a single planet to cause, and after years of additional observations, astronomers determined that whatever the unseen subject was, it possessed a mass greater than half the sun.

“The object’s unusual combination of high mass and dim light left only one plausible explanation: it was the remains of a dead star,” explained Charles-Antoine Parent, a University of Montreal astronomer and study co-author.

Possible suspects included a neutron star and even a secret black hole, but some assistance from the Gemini North telescope also on Mauna Kea finally confirmed its identity: a close-orbiting white dwarf. This complicated the situation. Astronomers previously discovered another white dwarf circling the red dwarf at a much greater distance. Taken altogether, that made three stars existing in a single system. The grouping is now known as Welopō‘ai, a Hawaiian phrase that roughly translates to “path of family traits” in reference to the stars’ shared relationships. According to researchers, no other comparable example can be found within 100 light-years of Earth.

However, Welopō‘ai still doesn’t quite add up. The red dwarf’s nearest companion was about 40 percent more massive than our sun prior to transforming into a white dwarf. When it did, it would have expanded hundreds of times its original size. Previously documented systems featuring these dynamics entailed the two stars falling into an even tighter orbit, or even merging. Despite this, Welopō‘ai’s red dwarf is still there and in a strikingly stable, wide orbit with the closest white dwarf. The team now plans to continue observing their discovery to learn as much as possible about the triple-star system, and possibly figure out how it formed in the first place.

“Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises,” added study co-author and astronomer, Étienne Artigau.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a latest patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

According to recent reports, the Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

It has been revealed that the journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The issue encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing upcoming Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently unveiled that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest-for-2026 Ferrari 296 Speciale is a sharper, faster, and more track-oriented variant of the brand’s V-6 supercar—but that doesn’t mean it is the only high-performance variant of the car that Ferrari will build. In a somewhat surprising break from recent tradition, Ferrari is also going to make a Challenge Stradale variant of the 296 to sell alongside the Speciale.

As the name suggests, the Challenge Stradale is a road-going variant of the 296 that shares a lot in common with the race car currently used in various Ferrari Challenge series. Specifically, its aerodynamic elements are strikingly similar to the upcoming 296 Challenge Evo, which was revealed alongside the new road car on November 21. The massive rear wing, front dive planes, and aggressive rear splitter are all extremely similar to design elements seen on that race car.

Sources indicate that those components combine to create a massive 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 miles per hour, an increase of 72 percent over the 296 GTB that won Road & Track Performance Car of the Year in 2024. Downforce is also up 401 lbs at that speed on the 296 Speciale, an increase of 29 percent.

It has been revealed that the removal of the hybrid system means a reduction in power, dropping from a combined system output of 819 horsepower in the 296 GTB to an engine-only output of 670 hp in the Challenge Stradale. The simplified powertrain and stripped out interior mean serious reductions in weight to match, though; the Challenge Stradale is 309 lbs lighter than the GTB and 176 lbs lighter than the Speciale.

Sources indicate that does the reduction in weight and increase in downforce make the 296 Challenge Stradale faster than the hybrid 296 Speciale already on the market? Not necessarily. Ferrari claims the Challenge Stradale is half a second a lap faster at its Fiorano test track, but marginally slower at a high-speed circuit like Monza. The more powerful Speciale should be quicker on other tracks with the on-throttle time necessary to allow the hybrid to stretch its legs, while the lighter Challenge Stradale should have the advantage on more technical circuits with more off-throttle time.

The other major differentiation between the Speciale and the Challenge Stradale is availability. While that other high-end 296 variant was a limited-run model, Ferrari stresses that the Challenge Stradale is a part of its regular lineup, and should be more available to buyers. It remains a Ferrari, so the market is unlikely to be flooded with 296s with massive wings in the years to come, but by supercar standards, it should be relatively attainable.

According to recent reports, ferrari has not yet revealed a price for the American market, but the brand indicates that it should start at the equivalent of just under $320,000 in Italy, including value-added tax. Prices in one region do not necessarily translate directly to another, but that number would leave the 296 Challenge Stradale in the general range of the similarly track-focused likes of Porsche’s 911 GT3 RS and Ford’s Mustang GTD.

3 Things to Do When Your Adult Child Pulls Away

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son.
  • This hurt, Mom soon added, "But I had no idea what to do next." This client elaborated that her fingers led her to compose and immediately delete five responses prior to sending them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 27, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son. The text was just a photo of her son's dog wearing (or at least trying to wear) a cap of a major league baseball team. She said, "Dr. Jeff, it's been two months since I last heard from him, and of course, I immediately smiled when I saw the pic.".

This hurt, Mom soon added, "But I had no idea what to do next." This client elaborated that her fingers led her to compose and immediately delete five responses prior to sending them. She added, "No matter what I do, he will pull away again, anyway.".

Industry observers note that the client above was struggling with how to respond after a long lag in communication with her adult child. She didn't know whether to joke about the cute picture, or tell her son she missed him, or ask further about Thanksgiving. For any parents in similar situations, it can be maddening to feel unsure about how to respond.

According to recent reports, and, if you have not spoken to your adult child for over six months or even years, the absence of that relationship has a huge, seemingly constant presence. By this I mean that often in these partial or full-on estrangement situations, the reality is that minimal or no contact does not take away from the internal emotional upheaval that comes from the desire to reconnect.

Industry observers note that it is easy to feel helpless in the face of not seeing your adult child or not having the level of connection that you value. In my parent coaching work, I encourage parents to focus on three things they can do no matter how long it's been since they last heard their grown child's voice.

Finish this sentence: "What I miss most about my grown child today is__________." Some parents might reply that they wish they knew how their son was doing. Maybe, as in the early example of the dog photo, a parent misses lighter moments of laughter. Maybe a song reminds you of your adult child.

Recent findings suggest that identifying what you miss is tangible and healthy because it helps you process difficult feelings like sadness, disappointment, nostalgia, or loneliness. For example, that treasured memory of you and your daughter going for a ride and belting out a shared favorite song may weigh heavily on your mind. Consider sharing these thoughts with trusted relatives, friends, a therapist, or a parent coach. Sometimes it helps to have someone just say, "Tell me more.".

Some parents have been deeply hurt by how their adult child has treated them, and yes, sometimes the reasons for the distance are unclear, and this can feel maddening. At the same time, if you genuinely regret anything you said or did, you can be specific about what you're apologizing for while still honoring your own experience of what happened.

Consider your adult daughter saying to you, "When I tell you what bothered me that you did when I was growing up, you kept twisting it to make it my fault and giving me advice." You may remember trying to help. But hold on, because, at the same time, maybe you can recall trying to give her advice when she remarked, "Dad, can I finish my point?".

Looking at your own behaviors in this way gives you an honest point of reflection to start. You could then say, "I've been reflecting on times I rushed in to give you advice, and it got in the way of better understanding what you were going through, and I'm sorry." This type of dialogue not only shows that you are taking responsibility, but you are also modeling self-awareness to your adult child.

Recent findings suggest that in my book, You Ruined My Life—Now You Owe Me!, I explore how easily a parent's regret can turn into a feeling of indebtedness. In the parent coaching trenches, I have seen how tempting it is for parents to promise their adult children something to bring them closer. Please keep in mind that you can offer a sincere apology and still take your time to decide what you can reasonably do or give. For parents who are totally out of contact, I suggest you write down what you regret and keep it private.

Industry observers note that this third point is really hard for parents missing their adult children. If several messages go unanswered, give your adult child room to reach out. If they asked for no contact, honor that request. Believe it or not, adult children in these situations often share with me that they still love and even miss their parents, even when they outwardly state they want no contact. Just remember what I wrote above: The absence of contact still has a great presence in both your mind and that of your adult child.

Toyota just built a tiny folding electric bike to fit in your trunk

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota is getting into electric bikes.
  • The Japanese automotive giant has unveiled the BKE Concept, a tiny folding electric two-wheeler designed to serve as a compact companion vehicle for short trips, outdoor adventures, and last-mile transportation.
  • Recent findings suggest that and when Toyota notes compact, it means it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is getting into electric bikes. Well, sort of.

The Japanese automotive giant has unveiled the BKE Concept, a tiny folding electric two-wheeler designed to serve as a compact companion vehicle for short trips, outdoor adventures, and last-mile transportation.

Recent findings suggest that and when Toyota notes compact, it means it. The little electric ride can reportedly fold up in around 30 seconds and become small enough to fit inside the trunk of the brand’s GR86 sports car. Think of it like Toyota’s take on the Motocompacto.

The BKE Concept was unveiled as part of the newly revived Scion by Toyota brand, which the manufacturer is positioning less as the return of the quirky youth-oriented car brand many Americans remember and more as a sort of experimental mobility laboratory.

It has been revealed that toyota calls the latest Scion a “freedom lab” where the organization can explore vehicles and mobility concepts that don’t necessarily fit neatly into its conventional automotive lineup. Alongside the BKE, Toyota highlighted its KEI-01 ultra-compact utility truck and a hybrid side-by-side.

But perhaps unsurprisingly for me, it’s the tiny electric two-wheeler that caught my attention.

And I should point out here that while Toyota refers to it as an “electric bike” in its own brand literature, the lack of pedals means that the cute little two-wheeler is not going to qualify as an electric bicycle in Europe or North America. The moniker means it merely slots into the broader electric bike category that encompasses everything from electric bicycles to scooters and motorcycles. In essence, the BKE is more or less a small seated e-scooter, sometimes referred to as a “no-ped”.

Despite looking like the kind of concept vehicle that might have been whipped up for an auto show, Toyota says the BKE has actually been under development for several years.

A small team of chassis and electrical engineers has reportedly been testing and refining the design based on real-world use and feedback.

The basic idea came from a fairly simple question: How could Toyota make short-distance mobility easier and integrate it more seamlessly into everyday life?

The result is essentially a secondary vehicle designed to travel inside your primary vehicle.

Toyota specifically highlights camping, errands, last-mile transportation, and even using the BKE as a pit bike alongside a GR86. The bike can also be recharged from the 110V AC outlets found in many Toyota vehicles, meaning the car carrying it can effectively serve as its mobile charging station.

Industry observers note that believe it or not, Toyota Chairman Akio Toyoda has apparently been involved in the testing process himself. Toyoda attracted attention after riding a similar small electric mobility device around the 2025 Japan Mobility Show, and Toyota claims his experience riding prototypes has even resulted in design changes.

After Toyoda complained about getting splashed while riding through puddles, for example, engineers enlarged the rear fender.

It’s a small detail, but it’s also a pretty textbook example of Toyota’s famous kaizen philosophy of continuous improvement.

Here’s where things get a little frustrating for those of us who want to know what the BKE can actually do.

Toyota hasn’t revealed the motor power, battery capacity, range, top speed, or even the vehicle’s weight. There’s also no pricing because, for now, there’s nothing to buy.

Toyota is referring to the BKE strictly as a concept and hasn’t announced production aims or a timetable for bringing it to market.

But the fact that Toyota says a small engineering team has spent several years developing and testing the BKE makes it more interesting than your typical one-off styling exercise.

And the underlying idea makes a lot of sense.

Industry observers note that I’m obviously a significant believer in matching the vehicle to the trip. Taking a 4,000-pound car several miles to move one person isn’t always the most efficient solution, and a compact electric two-wheeler gives drivers an easy way to leave the larger vehicle behind for those shorter trips.

Toyota itself makes essentially the same argument, saying that using smaller vehicles for shorter journeys could reduce emissions by better matching the vehicle to the task.

There’s also something amusingly circular about one of the world’s largest automakers arriving at the conclusion that sometimes the best vehicle for a trip is a tiny electric bike.

But hey, I’ll take it. Now Toyota just needs to actually build the thing – and preferably tell us how fast it goes first.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The RESET for Remission trial, presented at the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) Annual Meeting and published in The Lancet Regional Health Americas on October 1, found that more than half of adults with early onset type 2 diabetes entered remission after six months on a low calorie diet and supervised exercise program.
  • Early onset type 2 diabetes is when the condition is diagnosed before age 45.
  • Those with early onset type 2 diabetes may be at a higher risk of complications like long-term damage to the capillaries (microvascular complications), adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and earlier death.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The RESET for Remission trial, presented at the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) Annual Meeting and published in The Lancet Regional Health Americas on October 1, found that more than half of adults with early onset type 2 diabetes entered remission after six months on a low calorie diet and supervised exercise program.

Early onset type 2 diabetes is when the condition is diagnosed before age 45.

Those with early onset type 2 diabetes may be at a higher risk of complications like long-term damage to the capillaries (microvascular complications), adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and earlier death.

Typical treatment for early onset type 2 diabetes is often a combination of lifestyle changes, like diet and exercise, and medications.

However, this latest study suggests that a supervised low calorie diet and exercise program may help some people with early onset type 2 diabetes enter remission.

The RESET for Remission trial included 96 adults from England and Canada who were between the ages of 18 and 45, had early onset type 2 diabetes, obesity, and were not on insulin treatment.

The participants had an average age of 38 and an average body mass index (BMI) of 35.2 kg/m2. They were randomized into a control group that received usual care alone and the intervention group, which ate a low calorie diet and participated in supervised exercise programs.

During the first 12 weeks, participants in the intervention group followed an 800–900-calorie-per-day diet and completed twice-weekly supervised aerobic and resistance exercise sessions, along with one independent exercise session per week.

For weeks 13–24, they transitioned to a weight-maintenance diet and independent exercise.

Both groups were supervised by physicians, and the intervention group was also closely supervised by licensed dietitians.

It has been revealed that the low calorie diet consisted of 30% protein, 50% carbohydrate, and 20% fat. Participants were also encouraged to drink at least 2 liters of calorie-free fluids per day and given access to a fiber-based laxative as needed.

Recent findings suggest that in the first two weeks, all meals were replaced with specially formulated nutritional products (Optifast). Then, in weeks 3–12, the participants maintained the same calorie intake but had more flexibility in their food choices.

This second phase of the diet included one conventional meal per day, with daily intake targets that included protein, fruit, and vegetables. Typically, this meant 60 to 90 grams of protein from all sources combined, one portion of fruit, and two portions of non-starchy vegetables.

At the end of 24 weeks, 54% of the intervention group entered remission of type 2 diabetes, compared with only 4% in the control group. Researchers defined remission as an HbA1c level below 6.5% without glucose-lowering medication for at least 12 weeks.

In a recent development, “This study proves what most physicians have advocated for quite some time. Clearly, diet and exercise can work to improve or even resolve diabetes,” David Cutler, MD, board certified family medicine physician at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline.

Sources indicate that cutler also added that this study provides a clear example of how difficult it can be to enter diabetes remission with diet and exercise alone. He stated that the small number of participants in the study also makes him wonder if these findings can be applied to all populations.

Another limitation of this study, as Cutler pointed out, was that the strict dietary limits imposed on study participants would be very difficult for the average adult to adhere to.

The study also followed participants for only six months, so it’s unclear how many would remain in remission over the longer term.

“It is worth trying diet and exercise first because they can work to achieve meaningful weight loss and remission of diabetes,” he stated.

It may be possible to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes by:.

The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) notes that losing 5%–7% of your body weight can help reduce your risk of type 2 diabetes.

Early onset type 2 diabetes is a growing problem worldwide, coinciding with the rise of obesity.

Research from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) projects that the number of people in the United States under age 20 with type 2 diabetes could reach 220,000 by 2060. This is an increase of 700%.

People diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at a younger age face more decades of living with the condition, along with a higher risk of developing complications earlier in life and reduced life expectancy. These complications can develop as early as midlife and include:.

Speak with a healthcare professional about your risk of type 2 diabetes and changes you might be able to make in order to prevent or delay diagnosis.

A later diagnosis can help reduce the risk of some complications of the condition.

Arc Raiders patch nerfs the Deadline mine, ends the menace of the Venator

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that arc Raiders has received a fresh update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks.
  • Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the latest “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.
  • That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that arc Raiders has received a fresh update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the latest “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s update, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

It has been revealed that another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

It has been revealed that the patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

Check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. You should also learn what all the different Map Conditions do in Arc Raiders, and how to best make use of each of them.

Tesla Cybertruck’s already impressive turning radius gets even tighter

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is rolling out an update that makes the Cybertruck turn even tighter, improving on what was already one of the best turning radiuses you can get in a full-size pickup.
  • It only works on 2027 model year Cybertrucks, and Tesla plans to stop building the truck by the end of next summer.
  • Tesla’s official Cybertruck account posted a short drone video early Saturday showing a truck doing circles in a parking lot, with a “before” and “after” comparison of its turning path.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is rolling out an update that makes the Cybertruck turn even tighter, improving on what was already one of the best turning radiuses you can get in a full-size pickup.

But there’s a catch. It only works on 2027 model year Cybertrucks, and Tesla plans to stop building the truck by the end of next summer.

Tesla’s official Cybertruck account posted a short drone video early Saturday showing a truck doing circles in a parking lot, with a “before” and “after” comparison of its turning path. “Even tighter turns now rolling out to latest Cybertrucks,” the account wrote.

In a follow-up post, Tesla noted the improvement requires software version 2026.44 or newer and “only applies to model year 2027 Cybertrucks.”.

It's not the size … it's how you maneuver itEven tighter turns now rolling out to upcoming Cybertrucks pic.twitter.com/FuNoox4ax0.

In a recent development, tesla didn’t share a new turning circle figure. In the video, the “after” circle is visibly smaller than the “before” one by what looks to be at least a foot.

Recent findings suggest that the Cybertruck’s maneuverability comes from its rear-wheel steering paired with steer-by-wire. At low speeds, the rear wheels turn opposite to the fronts, which shrinks the space the truck needs to make a U-turn. We’ve been tracking the Cybertruck’s four-wheel steering since the prototype days, when Tesla was showing it off in parking garages.

Even before this update, the results were impressive. Tesla’s owner’s manual lists the Cybertruck’s curb-to-curb turning circle at about 43.5 ft (13.25 m). That beats the Ford F-150 Lightning at roughly 47.8 ft and the Rivian R1T at 44.9 ft, and it’s within about 4 ft of a Model Y. Not bad for a 6,600-lb truck that’s nearly 19 feet long.

And Tesla always stated there was more to come. At launch, the rear wheels turned only about 3 degrees. In early 2024, a Tesla engineer said a software update would push that to 10 degrees, and Elon Musk said the organization had improvements in the works to “tighten the turning circle significantly.”.

Tesla hasn’t mentioned whether this upgrade delivers the full 10 degrees, or why it’s limited to 2027 trucks. If it comes down to hardware, owners of earlier Cybertrucks who were counting on this as an over-the-air upgrade are out of luck.

Credit where it’s due. The turning circle is one of the best things about the Cybertruck, and anyone who has driven one knows it. Steer-by-wire combined with rear-wheel steering is real engineering, and other vehicles are just starting to get that combo a couple years after Cybertruck had it. Making it even better is a nice revision.

But it’s hard to get excited about it.

And 39.4 feet turning circle for the Cadillac Escalade which also has rear wheel steering. As does the iX5 (39.7'), MB GLC (36.7') and EQS (35.8'), the Lucid Gravity (38.4), Hummer 37.4', Cayenne (38.4) and a around two dozen other vehicles on the market today. So maybe this is not such big news after all?

Sources indicate that earlier this month, Musk revealed that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas to make room for Cybercab. He has since pushed the end date to the end of summer 2027 to work through an “order backlog.” We estimate Tesla is delivering about 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks a quarter, roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year it planned for.

Recent findings suggest that so Tesla is improving a 2027 model year truck that it will stop making next summer. And since Tesla now only sells the $109,990 Cyberbeast, the people getting this upgrade are the few still buying the most expensive Cybertruck in its final months. It does nothing about what actually sank the truck: pricing that never came close to the $39,900 promised in 2019, range and towing that fell short, and a design most truck buyers never warmed up to.

It’s a cool engineering flex on a product with an expiration date. If Tesla had delivered this kind of polish on the $40,000 truck it promised, would we be writing the Cybertruck’s obituary right now?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Max Verstappen started on pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday evening and held the lead at one point on every lap, but the race was far more thrilling than that would let on.
  • Verstappen qualified second and inherited pole after pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli received a five-place grid penalty.
  • At the start, Max Verstappen took the lead from George Russell and kept his elbows out as he had the hardest spot on the track, punching through the crisp air with no help from a slipstream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Verstappen started on pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday evening and held the lead at one point on every lap, but the race was far more thrilling than that would let on.

Verstappen qualified second and inherited pole after pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli received a five-place grid penalty.

At the start, Max Verstappen took the lead from George Russell and kept his elbows out as he had the hardest spot on the track, punching through the crisp air with no help from a slipstream.

It has been revealed that on the second lap of the race, Russell, in a much faster Mercedes, passed Verstappen in the final corners coming off the Las Vegas Strip straight, then lost the lead before the first corner of the next lap. He would repeat this multiple times throughout the first half of the Grand Prix.

The race recorded a record 35 lead changes, but no one could cement a run past Verstappen.

With Verstappen slowing the field behind him, the first 10 laps of the race found the top three within one second and the top ten within less than 4.5 seconds.

It has been revealed that on lap 20, Sergio Perez tried to make a pick on Rafeal Camera and the Haas, and Cadillac ended up tangled in the barrier, bringing out a full safety car. In a normal race, this would’ve neutralized the race, but with everyone still running bunched up, it just sent the field all together to the pits, leading to teams double-stacking against each other.

Hamilton was the biggest loser at the pit stop, having to serve a 10-second penalty that was not yet shared with him for a battle with Norris that he thought was just.

Hamilton was kept out while everyone else pitted to clear space for Charles Leclerc and was told about his penalty.

“Ah, that’s shit. If I turned in, we would’ve crashed.”.

It has been revealed that under the safety car, Arvid Lindblad spun on cold tires to end his campaign for his first-ever podium. Arvid had his best starting spot of fifth for the Grand Prix and ran as high as third, while the Red Bulls on his sister team ran 1-2; he fell out of the points with the mistake.

Sources indicate that shortly after racing resumed, Isack Hadjar, who challenged his teammate Verstappen for the lead in the first half of the race and often put in the hardest position between the leader and the charging field, hit debris on the track and damaged his front wing. Hadjar pitted and finished outside the points as well.

With Red Bull and VCARB drivers out of contention, the door reopened for the Mercedes as Kimi Antonelli made his way into the picture following his grid drop, and Russell never left.

With two laps to go, Antonelli led Russell as the teammate fought for second; in turn 5, Russell went for the pass, overcommitted, and slid into the barrier.

Verstappen laughed on from ahead following a weekend of tension between the front-row starters.

Antonelli fell away from the lead battle on the penultimate lap with an internal issue and would come home fourth.

According to recent reports, in the mayhem, the McLarens saw their luck change at Las Vegas. Following this double disqualification while battling for the championship last year, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri walked away with a shocking first double podium of the season.

“I led for about 15 seconds, so I’m very proud,” Norris joked.

Antonelli was followed by Pierre Gasly, Franco Colapinto, Lewis Hamilton, Carlos Sainz, George Russell and Charles Leclerc in the points-paying positions.

#224514. The Courage to Question Our Own Certainty
